verdict.rationale: Obsidian's core architecture (local plain-text Markdown storage, optional end-to-end encrypted Sync where 'no one — not even the Obsidian team — can access your notes') strongly implies user data isn't harvested for AI training since it never leaves the user's control by default. However, there is no explicit vendor statement or policy addressing AI-training use of data, and Obsidian's own docs admit community plugins have unrestricted filesystem/network access with no sandboxing, meaning third-party plugins (e.g. AI plugins) could still exfiltrate data outside Obsidian's control. Missing for 10: an explicit anti-AI-training data policy statement, and any assurance/controls over what community AI plugins do with vault data.
